jobs.title: Sr. Analyst, Financial Systems: Oracle GL and Financial Close
jobs.excerpt: Alignment Health is breaking the mold in conventional health care, committed to serving seniors and those who need it most: the chronically ill and frail.
jobs.description:
Alignment Health is breaking the mold in conventional health care, committed to serving seniors and those who need it most: the chronically ill and frail. It takes an entire team of passionate and caring people, united in our mission to put the senior first.We have built a team of talented and experienced people who are passionate about transforming the lives of the seniors we serve. In this fast-growing company, you will find ample room for growth and innovation alongside the Alignment Health community. Working at Alignment Health provides an opportunity to do work that really matters, not only changing lives but saving them. Together.

The Senior Analyst, Oracle GL & Financial Close Systems (remote)is the technical subject matter expert responsible for the stability, configuration, and optimization of Oracle Cloud Financials' General Ledger and Financial Close environment — the operational core that ensures every dollar is accurately recorded, reconciled, and reported in our Medicare Advantage business. Working as the primary technical partner to the Corporate Accounting team, this role ensures that period-end close cycles run flawlessly, sub-ledger integrations are intact, and financial reporting meets the accuracy standards required by US GAAP, SOX, and CMS regulatory frameworks.

In a Medicare Advantage organization, the stakes of GL and close accuracy are uniquely high — from medical cost accruals and risk adjustment entries to intercompany eliminations across plan entities — making this role essential to both our financial integrity and our ability to meet regulatory reporting deadlines with confidence.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

May include but are not limited to

1. Provide Expert Technical Support for Financial Close Cycles
Serve as the primary technical resource for the Corporate Accounting team during Monthly, Quarterly, and Year-End close cycles, ensuring that all close activitiesexecuteon time and without system-related disruption. Troubleshoot complex journal entry issues — includingautomated accruals, recurring journals, cross-validation rule failures, and sub-ledger posting errors — resolving root causes before theyimpactclose timelines or financial statement accuracy.

2. Maintain General Ledger Configuration and System Setup
Own and maintain all GL system configurations — including Chart of Accounts (COA) mapping, Accounting Calendars, Ledger Sets, Data Access Sets, and cross-validation rules — ensuring the Oracle General Ledger remains correctly structured as the business grows and evolves. Manage technical workflows supporting multi-currency translations, revaluations, and intercompany consolidations and eliminations across Medicare Advantage plan entities.

3. Automate and Optimize the Financial Close Process
Identify and implement automation opportunities within the Oracle Close Monitor and broader close workflow to reduce manual cycle time,eliminaterepetitive tasks, and increase the reliability of period-end execution. Apply scripting and automation tools — including Python, PowerShell, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles — to streamline GL processes and build a more resilient, repeatable close environment.

4. Manage Sub-Ledger Integrations and Data Integrity
Monitor and troubleshoot inbound interfaces from Oracle sub-ledgers (AP, AR, Fixed Assets, Payroll) and external third-party systems — including healthcare-specific platforms — ensuring that all transactions post accurately and completely to the General Ledger. Build andmaintaintechnical queries (SQL) to support the Corporate Accounting team in reconciling sub-ledger balances to the GL andresolvingout-of-balance conditions rapidly.

5. Develop and Sustain Financial Reporting Infrastructure
Build, maintain, and optimize complex financial reports using Oracle Financial Reporting Studio (FRS), Smart View, and OTBI (Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence), providing Corporate Accounting and Finance leadership with the accurate, timely reporting they need to manage the business and meet external obligations. Ensure that reporting workloads are query-optimizedso they do not degrade transaction processing performance during peak financial close periods.

6. Enforce Compliance, Security, and Audit Readiness
Maintain Segregation of Duties (SoD) controls within the GL module and support internal and external audit requests by providing system logs, configuration snapshots, and data lineage documentation. Ensure all GL configurations, journal entries, and system changes are documented in alignment with SOX internal control requirements and CMS financial reporting standards applicable to Medicare Advantage organizations.

Job Description Summary:

The Payroll Manager provides functional oversight and strategic leadership for payroll operations, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant payroll administration. This position establishes payroll priorities, policies, controls, and performance expectations; oversees payroll tax compliance, financial reconciliation, reporting, systems, vendor relationships, and year-end activities; and leads the payroll team in identifying and managing operational risks and process improvements. The Payroll Manager partners with Human Resources, Finance, and other stakeholders to support effective payroll governance and business operations.

Job Description:

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following (other duties may be assigned):

Leadership and Payroll Oversight

  • Oversee the end-to-end payroll function, establishing priorities, operating standards, and strategic direction to support accurate and timely payroll delivery.
  • Lead, coach, and evaluate payroll team members; establish accountability for performance, capacity, deadlines, and quality of work.
  • Provide guidance and escalation support on complex payroll matters and ensure timely resolution of significant operational issues.

Compliance, Tax and Risk Management

  • Oversee payroll tax compliance, required filings, and deposits across applicable federal, state, and local jurisdictions.
  • Establish and maintain payroll controls, compliance procedures, and audit readiness; assess payroll-related risks and implement corrective measures.
  • Monitor changes in payroll laws and regulations, evaluate their impact, and direct necessary process or policy updates.

Finance Partnership and Reconciliation

  • Partner with Finance on payroll-to-general-ledger reconciliation, financial reporting, and resolution of material variances.
  • Oversee payroll funding, accruals, and related financial controls; address significant reconciliation issues and provide accurate payroll information for financial reporting.

Projects, Systems and Process Improvement

  • Lead major payroll projects, including system implementations, upgrades, and changes, establishing project priorities, governance, and accountability.
  • Establish payroll systems strategy and oversee payroll vendor relationships, service delivery, and performance.
  • Identify and implement process improvements that strengthen payroll accuracy, compliance, controls, and operational efficiency.

Reporting and Governance

  • Establish, maintain, and update payroll policies, procedures, and internal controls.
  • Define payroll key performance indicators, monitor team and operational performance, and provide management reporting on trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.

Year-End Oversight

  • Lead the year-end payroll process, establishing timelines, deliverables, and cross-functional responsibilities.
  • Oversee the review and approval of Forms W-2 and related year-end reporting to ensure accurate and timely completion.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders and vendors to manage year-end dependencies, resolve issues, and meet reporting deadlines.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Requirements:

jobs.excerpt: About UsSince 1989, SHI International Corp.  has helped organizations change the world through technology.
jobs.description:
About Us

Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services.

Over 17,000 organizations worldwide rely on SHI’s concierge approach to help them solve what’s next. But the heartbeat of SHI is our employees – all 7,000 of them. If you join our team, you’ll enjoy:

  • Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S.

  • Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities.

  • Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family.

  • World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours.

Job Summary

The Solutions Engineer – Agents & Automation is responsible for building and delivering enterprise agent solutions using Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent Builder. This role also supports agent governance and lifecycle management through Agent 365.

This hands-on role focuses on implementing declarative and prompt-based agents, custom-engine agents, and enterprise integrations while helping customers establish governed, scalable environments for agent development and lifecycle management. Responsibilities include configuring Power Platform environment strategies, implementing zoned governance, developing agents across Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry, and supporting secure agent operations across Power Platform and Azure.

The role also supports Agent 365 onboarding activities, including configuring conditional access policies, enabling agent lifecycle workflows, and implementing key governance and security capabilities across the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft Entra Agent ID, Microsoft Purview, and Microsoft Defender.

The Solutions Engineer translates designs into production-ready solutions, drives consistent and secure delivery, and accelerates reuse through proven patterns. The role sits at the intersection of AI innovation, human experience, and responsible AI enablement, helping organizations establish scalable, governed agent capabilities while contributing to the continued evolution of SHI’s Microsoft Services practice.

Role Description


Agent Architecture and Development

  • Act as the technical subject matter expert (SME) for workforce agent solution development across Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry, including first-party agents, declarative agents, and custom-engine agent development.
  • Build and deploy custom-engine agents in Microsoft Foundry, including model selection, orchestration, grounding, evaluation, tool and function integration, and connectivity with Copilot Studio and enterprise systems.
  • Demonstrate familiarity with the Microsoft IQ stack, including Work IQ, Foundry IQ, and Fabric IQ, and its role in enabling intelligent agent experiences through knowledge, grounding, orchestration, evaluation, and integration patterns across Microsoft agent platforms.
  • Guide SHI customers through hands-on agent solution delivery, custom DLP policies, environment and AI readiness assessments, use case identification, and governance of enterprise agent platforms.
  • Lead agent governance implementation, including environment readiness, Power Platform environment strategy, zoned governance, prerequisite validation, platform enablement, and deployment planning across Power Platform, Azure, and related services, using Power Platform Pipelines, Azure DevOps, and GitHub Actions where appropriate.
  • Design and implement agent security and compliance controls as part of Agent 365 onboarding, using Microsoft Purview for labels, DLP, and eDiscovery; Microsoft Defender for threat visibility; and Microsoft Entra Agent ID for identity, conditional access, and least-privilege access.
  • Establish enterprise agent governance through environment strategy (DEV/UAT/PROD), managed environments, ALM/pipelines, connector governance, solution packaging, auditing, and lifecycle management for Copilot Studio agents and agent flows.
  • Own the end-to-end implementation of agent solutions by translating business requirements into workflows, automations, integrations, and extensibility patterns across Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI Services, and Power Platform.
  • Implement Power Platform governance and ALM capabilities, including managed environments, environment groups, DLP policies, pipeline configuration, approval workflows, Copilot Studio Kit setup, and administrator enablement.
  • Define fit-for-purpose agent architectures that align platform capabilities, custom agent logic, integrations, orchestration patterns, and automation workflows with customer requirements.
  • Implement secure and governed agent environments, including identity, data access, compliance, monitoring, and lifecycle management using Microsoft security and governance services.
  • Guide teams on agent design, governance, evaluation, observability, audit readiness, and operational best practices, including analytics, feedback loops, and continuous improvement.
  • Develop and maintain reusable technical assets, including reference architectures, design patterns, solution templates, and implementation guides for Copilot and agent services.
  • Help customers evaluate and adopt emerging Microsoft Frontier agent capabilities, including prebuilt Microsoft agents, Microsoft Foundry features, Copilot Studio capabilities, and new Agent 365 platform services.
  • Apply FinOps practices for agents and AI workloads, including Copilot Credit planning, cost-benefit analysis, usage forecasting, model selection, consumption monitoring, and cost optimization across Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, and related Microsoft AI services.
  • Work effectively in Visual Studio Code and use GitHub Copilot and other coding assistants to build, extend, and troubleshoot solutions for Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry-hosted agents, and the Agent 365 SDK.
  • Demonstrate familiarity with agent development frameworks such as Microsoft Agent Framework to support extensible, code-first agent development patterns across Microsoft agent platforms.
  • Perform agent evaluations in Microsoft Foundry and Copilot Studio, including testing agent responses, validating grounding quality, measuring effectiveness, and using evaluation results to improve agent behavior, reliability, and user experience.
  • Design agent grounding and retrieval architectures using enterprise data sources, connectors, knowledge sources, Azure AI Search, Microsoft Graph, MCP Servers, Dataverse, and secure data access patterns.
  • Implement responsible AI and safety controls for agent solutions, including safety testing, evaluation criteria, risk review, content moderation considerations, human oversight patterns, and continuous improvement.

Behaviors and Competencies

  • Customer Communication: Clearly explain complex Microsoft AI, Copilot, agent, governance, and automation concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Presentation and Facilitation: Design and deliver engaging presentations, workshops, and technical discussions tailored to the audience, business need, and delivery context.
  • Technical Judgment: Evaluate requirements, constraints, risks, and platform capabilities to recommend practical, scalable, and supportable agent solutions.
  • Problem Solving: Proactively identify issues, dependencies, and delivery risks and recommend clear options and corrective actions.
  • Detail Orientation: Manage complex implementation tasks with attention to configuration accuracy, governance requirements, documentation quality, and delivery consistency.
  • Organization and Follow-Through: Coordinate multiple workstreams, track decisions and action items, and ensure commitments are completed on time.
  • Relationship Building: Build trust with customers, partners, Microsoft stakeholders, and internal delivery teams through reliable communication and collaborative execution.
  • Documentation and Reuse: Create clear documentation, implementation guides, design patterns, and reusable assets that improve delivery quality and operational efficiency.
  • Results Orientation: Drive work toward measurable outcomes while balancing customer value, technical quality, governance, and long-term supportability.

Skill Level Requirements


We are looking for candidates who demonstrate strength across the following areas. Deep expertise in every tool is not required, but experience across these capabilities is important for success. Candidates should not self-select out if they do not meet all of these requirements.


  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical, business, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Four or more years of experience delivering solutions on Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Azure, or related Microsoft cloud technologies, including hands-on experience with AI or agent-based solutions.
  • Practical experience developing production agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry, including first-party agent capabilities and custom-engine agents.
  • Experience designing or implementing declarative and embedded agent experiences across Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, and Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Fx, and configuration-based development patterns such as YAML.
  • Strong understanding of agent architecture, governance, security, and lifecycle management, including identity, compliance, monitoring, and operational controls across Power Platform Admin Center, Microsoft 365 admin center, Agent 365 control plane, Foundry control plane, and related services.
  • Proven ability to act as a technical advisor and SME, guiding solution design and implementation decisions across project teams.
  • Working knowledge of applied AI concepts, including prompt design, evaluation, monitoring, and responsible AI practices.
  • Familiarity with design-led or human-centered approaches as they apply to technical solution design and workflow modeling.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to translate business needs into scalable technical solutions.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Other Requirements

  • Ability to travel to SHI, Partner, and Customer events.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with sales, delivery, engineering, and leadership stakeholders.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and upskilling across Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, Agent 365, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, AI workloads, governance, and change and adoption best practices.
  • Strong ethical standards with disciplined adherence to data privacy, governance, compliance, and security policies.

Certification

Relevant certifications may include:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals (AB-900)
  • Power Platform Solutions Architect (PL-600)
  • Microsoft Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect (AB-100)
  • Microsoft Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-103)
  • Equivalent experience may be considered.

Personal Attributes

What Pula Will Bring to the Table

Asure Software helps small and mid-sized businesses grow by simplifying payroll, human resources, compliance, and workforce management. Our clients can choose the delivery model that works best for their business—from self-service technology to fully managed solutions and partner-enabled services.

About Fluent Software Group

Fluent Software Group acquires and grows vertical market software companies. Our portfolio businesses deliver mission-critical software to the industries they serve, and our Finance team provides the controllership, reporting, and M&A support that keeps the group scaling. As we continue to acquire, we are building a finance function that is technically excellent, systems-driven, and ahead of the curve on AI-enabled automation.

The Opportunity: Controller

The Portfolio Controller reports directly to the Portfolio Director of Finance and works as part of the broader Finance team. This is a technical role combining controllership, treasury, and compliance ownership. You will be the portfolio’s technical accounting specialist — owning the cash management process, ensuring robust internal controls and clean audit outcomes — while actively partnering with other department teams to raise reporting quality without becoming a bottleneck in day-to-day operations.

You will own the controllership and treasury function end-to-end: from intercompany reconciliation to IFRS 15 and 16, tax compliance, and cash management across your responsible businesses.

Location: Quebec, Ontario or Alberta (Remote)

International travel may be required for business process reviews and acquisition integration.

The salary range for this role is $100,000–$120,000 CAD per year, plus 10% annual bonus. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and location.

What You’ll Own

  • Own the preparation and review of all assigned business month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close deliverables, including the statement of cash flows and dividend declarations.
  • Own the treasury function, including monthly cash requirements reporting, banking administration, debt management, working capital planning, coordinating dividend payment and maintaining accurate cash visibility at all times.
  • Coordinate tax compliance obligations where required, specifically transfer pricing arrangements, corporate tax support, and compliance deadlines, consulting with external advisors as needed.
  • Serve as the technical accounting lead for assigned businesses, providing guidance on IFRS 15, IFRS 16, IFRS 3, consolidations, and other complex accounting matters.
  • Lead the intercompany reconciliation and recharges process across assigned businesses, including resolving complex discrepancies and improving consistency between entities.
  • Own and strengthen the internal control environment across the portfolio, identifying financial risks, addressing control gaps, and supporting clean audit outcomes.
  • Support acquisition integration from a technical accounting perspective, including step plan adherence, revenue recognition checklists, and PPA model review, as well as aligning newly acquired businesses with Fluent’s accounting policies and controls.
  • Manage a team of 2–3, ensuring tasks are appropriately delegated and team members are coached and developed, while maintaining accountability for the accuracy and quality of their work.
  • Partner with cross-functional leaders at the businesses and align priorities, financial risk, process improvements, and broader finance initiatives.

What We’re Looking For

  • A minimum of 7 years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including experience operating at a manager or controller level.
  • CPA, CA, or equivalent professional accounting qualification.
  • Previous experience operating at the manager level, with responsibility for overseeing key accounting processes and deliverables, including independently managing complex financial matters across multiple businesses or legal entities.
  • Proven people management or team leadership experience, including coaching, supporting, developing, and reviewing the work of team members.
  • Strong IFRS technical knowledge, specifically IFRS 15, IFRS 16, and IFRS 3, with essential consolidation accounting experience and exposure to complex intercompany transactions and internal controls.
  • Advanced Excel skills; demonstrated experience using AI tools (Claude, Copilot, or equivalent) to automate finance workflows; Python or Power Query experience is a strong advantage.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience in both public practice accounting and a private industry accounting environment
  • Previous experience within the software industry, particularly in a recurring revenue or SaaS environment.
  • Hands-on experience with NetSuite and Power BI

Why Fluent Software Group?

  • Entrepreneurial Energy: No two days look the same — you’ll work on meaningful problems with real business impact

As a Senior Accountant & Client Advisor, you will play a pivotal role in delivering technical excellence on accounting and tax work for our book of small and mid-sized business clients, paired with the client-facing judgment to translate that work into real advisory value. This is not a relationship-management role with light technical exposure — it's a technical accounting/tax seat that also owns the client relationship. You will personally prepare and review returns and financials, catch what the rest of the team misses, and only then move into onboarding, retention, and advisory conversations built on that technical foundation.

  • Personally prepare and/or review accounting and tax deliverables before they reach the client, catching errors early — this is hands-on technical work, not just oversight.

  • Hands-on experience actually preparing tax returns — not only reviewing or quality-checking them — for corporations, partnerships, LLCs, or individuals.

  • Comfortable serving as the technical backstop for a small team — reviewing work, catching errors, and coaching less-experienced team members.
  • Strong organizational skills; capable of managing a book of 40–60+ accounts without anything falling through the cracks.
  • Familiarity with Profit First by Mike Michalowicz, Built to Sell by John Warrilow, and Traction by Gino Wickman is a strong asset.

Our Values

  • Work Hard, Stay Humble — We bring our best to every project and keep our feet on the ground while doing it.

  • Keep it Fun & Lighthearted — Hard work is non-negotiable, but we know how to have a good time while we're at it.

Our Recruitment Process

Your application will be reviewed, and those moving to the next step will be asked to complete a brief 5-question one-way video interview where you will answer these questions on your own time via your webcam. Following that, successful candidates will be invited to take part in a series of 1-on-1 interviews.

Ethical and Cultural Sensitivity

jobs.description:
This is an internal role at Weekday. Not a role by a client.

  • Role type: Full time
  • Location: Remote
  • Working days: Monday–Saturday
  • Working with: The founders and the AE team

Weekday is an AI-native recruiting platform. We are backed by Y Combinator and Venture Highway (now General Catalyst). We have built the largest white-collar talent database in India and have built tools to run outbound recruiting campaigns to them.

About the role

You will own outbound sales to Indian startups. Not support it. Own it. You find the companies, you get in the door, you run the demo, you close, and you hand over a customer who knows exactly what they bought.

We have an AE team of three today. It works, and it closes. Now we need to scale it, and you will be a critical part of that. That means two things: you carry your own number from week one, and you help figure out what the team looks like at ten. What's repeatable, what isn't, what to write down, what to throw out. The people we hire after you will run on what you help build.

We sell to founders and heads of talent at startups that are hiring. They are busy, sceptical, and have been burned by recruiting agencies before. Your job is to show them, in one call, why a talent database of this size plus outbound campaigns gets them hires faster than anything else they've tried.

If you want a clean job description with neat boundaries, this isn't for you. If you want to be one of the people who scaled the sales engine at a profitable, venture-backed company, read on.

What you'll actually do

On any given day you might be:

  • Building your own target list of Indian startups that are hiring, and figuring out who the real decision-maker is
  • Running cold outbound across email, LinkedIn, and phone, and iterating on what actually gets a reply
  • Running demos that are built around the prospect's open roles, not a generic walkthrough of the product
  • Closing subscription deals and handling pricing, procurement, and the "let me think about it" that never comes back on its own
  • Handing closed accounts over to the delivery team cleanly, so the first month goes well and the renewal takes care of itself
  • Keeping the pipeline honest in the CRM, and reporting the numbers to the founders every week, including the ugly ones
  • Sitting with the other AEs to work out what's working across the team, and turning it into process the next hires can run on

You'll be measured on closed revenue and pipeline built. Not on activity, not on slides.

What we're looking for

  • You've sold B2B before, ideally to startups, ideally something a founder had to say yes to. You know what a real pipeline looks like.
  • You're comfortable with cold outbound. Not tolerant of it. Comfortable. You'd rather send fifty good emails than wait for a lead.
  • You can run a demo that feels like a conversation and ends with a next step.
  • You close. You ask for the deal, you handle the objection, and you don't confuse a friendly call with a sale.
  • You take ownership. When a number is yours, it moves, and nobody has to follow up with you.
  • You've seen a sales team grow, or you want to be the person who makes it grow. You think about the system, not just your own quota.
  • You understand the Indian startup ecosystem, who's hiring, who's raising, and who's about to need ten engineers in a hurry.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and a Monday–Saturday pace.

What you get

  • An early seat on a sales team that's about to scale, at a profitable, venture-backed company
  • Direct access to the founders and a say in pricing, positioning, and what we build next
  • A product with real pull: the largest white-collar talent database in India and outbound tooling that companies actually get hires from
  • A clear path to leading a team as the function grows, if you earn it
  • A front-row seat to how a startup gets built and run, and the track record to show for it when you build your own

Ready to Make a Real Impact? Join e-STORAGE!

Who We Are

Welcome to e-STORAGE, a proud member of the Canadian Solar Inc. (NASDAQ: CSIQ) family! To accelerate the world’s renewable energy transition and create a more sustainable, resilient energy future for everyone.

With our innovative SolBank lithium-iron phosphate battery technology and comprehensive project services, we’re not just building products we’re powering communities and making a difference worldwide.

Position Title: Technical Solutions Engineer
Department: Technical Solutions
Compensation: $85,000 - $135,000 + annual bonus (range varies depending on location; paid in local currency)
Reports To: Technical Solutions Manager
Location: Remote – Canada or USA

About the Role:

The Technical Solutions Engineer will play a key role in supporting the development, evaluation, and integration of utility-scale energy storage systems (ESS) with a focus on battery technology and performance in integrated systems. This role supports both internal product development and external solution customization, ensuring seamless operation and coordination between the Battery Product, Inverters, EMS and grid interface.

This position requires deep fluency in battery cell and pack-level degradation mechanisms, the ability to translate degradation curve behavior into commercial and contractual strategy (warranties, guarantees, storage/charging requirements), and the judgment to drive design and process improvements back into the product roadmap. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable building degradation models in Excel/Python, defending assumptions in front of an Independent Engineer, and sitting across the table from R&D to push for a design change.

This role supports both internal product development and external solution customization. For internally developed solutions, the engineer will work closely with R&D, global engineering to provide direct input on design features, validation strategies, and system sizing requirements. For externally procured products, the focus will be on leading technical due diligence, ensuring standards compliance, and transferring product knowledge to internal engineering, applications, and execution teams.

Responsibilities:

Technical Due Diligence and Product Development

  • Lead the technical review of new battery cells and sub-components being evaluated for integration into our solutions, including specs, drawings, sizing, certifications, and test results.
  • Work closely with procurement, product management, and R&D teams to support alignment between product design, supplier capabilities, and commercial rollout.
  • For internally developed products: collaborate with R&D and technical teams to support design development, interface definition, validation testing, and product roadmap alignment.
  • For externally sourced products: lead evaluation of technical specifications, certifications, and performance claims; ensure alignment with internal architecture and support cross-functional knowledge transfer.
  • Maintain traceability of vendor/product documentation, internal evaluations, and solutions status through internal tools and documentation systems.
  • Oversee the development and enhancement of internal engineering tools to support system modeling, product validation, and solution optimization efforts.
  • Support Independent Engineer (IE) reviews and customer-led technical due diligence by preparing documentation packages, addressing compliance concerns, and representing internal design rationale.
  • Monitor and interpret evolving product standards, test requirements, and performance expectations relevant to battery and energy solutions — including UL, IEEE, IEC, and other applicable regional or application-specific standards — and ensure alignment across internal designs and documentation.

Battery Performance & Degradation Strategy

  • Own and evolve degradation modeling methodology and strategy in externally facing degradation curves for product and system warranties.
  • Maintain and improve internal degradation and throughput tools (capacity models, throughput analysis, duty cycle tools etc.) ensuring accuracy across models, chemistries, and climate conditions.
  • Serve as the primary technical liaison between project and performance engineering and R&D, feeding field/factory degradation insights and failure trends back into cell selection, thermal management, and DC Block design decisions.
  • Monitor and interpret emerging battery chemistries and design (e.g., winding/stacking, blade cells, sodium-ion) for their degradation, safety, and warranty implications, and assess their fit against existing performance guarantee structures.

Cross-functional Support and Customization

  • Coordinate cross-functional communication to introduce new products to internal stakeholders, including engineering, project execution, and commercial teams.
  • Lead internal discussions with engineering, product, and software/controls teams to troubleshoot control strategies and support platform optimization.
  • Provide technical input and coordination for project-specific requirements, custom feature requests, or client-specific configurations.
  • Contribute to the development of internal documentation, reference templates, and knowledge-sharing tools that support consistent product execution across regions.
  • Collaborate closely with global R&D and applications engineering teams, to align on feature roadmaps and deployment readiness.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned by management.

Required Qualifications and Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, materials science, electrochemistry, or a related discipline; preference given to candidates with a postgraduate degree in engineering.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in engineering, R&D, or product management within battery storage, battery cell development, or related industries.
  • Direct experience in battery product development, cell testing, or energy storage applications is strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of LFP battery cells, DC Blocks, and Energy Storage Systems
  • Familiarity with key standards and certifications related to batteries and ESS products, including UL 9540, UL9540A, UL 1973, UN 38.3, IEC 62933, IEC 62619, and other applicable codes or testing standards.
  • Experience collaborating with international partners, particularly engineering or manufacturing teams across global time zones.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead or contribute to the development of internal engineering tools, system models, or automation processes.
  • Strong technical, analytical, and troubleshooting skills, with a hands-on approach to product validation and integration.
  • Proficiency in Mandarin is a plus but not required.

Key Competencies

  • Ability to collaborate effectively across diverse, cross-functional teams and international time zones.
  • Strong technical communication skills, with the ability to navigate discussions across internal teams and represent engineering topics in customer or Independent Engineer (IE) reviews — particularly in coordination with R&D counterparts across Asia, North America, and Europe.
  • Experience with product onboarding, technical documentation review, and vendor qualification processes is highly desirable.
  • Excellent organizational skills, and clear written and verbal communication across global teams.
  • Flexibility to travel, including international travel as required (up to 15%) for vendor assessments, integration testing, and industry events.

VP, Engineering

Northeast - Boston, NYC

OnCorps is the leading enterprise Agentic AI solution for middle and back-office automation. The company delivers production-ready AI agents that automate reconciliation, exception resolution, and oversight workflows for the world's largest asset managers, fund administrators and managed service providers.

OnCorps' agentic AI architecture enables fully autonomous processing of complex middle and back-office workflows while maintaining the transparency, control, and auditability required by global financial institutions. Clients rely on OnCorps to deliver measurable operational efficiency and accuracy improvements across mission critical processes.

With a rapidly growing customer base and increasing demand for scalable AI solutions in capital markets, OnCorps is expanding its senior management team to include a VP, Software Engineering to scale its platform and technical organization through the Company’s next phase of innovation and expansion.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a seasoned and visionary VP of Engineering to lead engineering execution, architecture, and operational delivery under the Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO). Reporting directly to the CPTO, the VP of Engineering will be responsible for leading our engineering functions, driving technical execution, scaling our AI-centric enterprise SaaS platform, and ensuring OnCorps continues to deliver trusted, secure, and high-performing AI solutions to the capital markets ecosystem.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical acumen in enterprise SaaS and AI platforms. We are seeking a VP of Engineering with demonstrated success leading distributed engineering teams and scaling AI-powered SaaS platforms. This leader must be fluent in modern AI development workflows and capable of building a fully AI-enabled engineering organization that effectively leverages coding agents, testing agents, and AI-assisted development tools to accelerate innovation and productivity.

The ideal candidate will operate as a player coach, aligning with OnCorps’ culture of builders and innovators.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Execution & Delivery

  • Drive day-to-day software development, engineering operations, and delivery velocity across engineering teams.
  • Partner closely with Product Management and Program Management to translate strategic product roadmaps into predictable, high-quality engineering sprints and releases.
  • Ensure rigorous engineering standards for agile development, release management, code quality, and cloud-native scalability.
  • Partner with the CPTO and senior leadership to set the direction for platform evolution, AI integration, and client scalability.
  • Stay ahead of technology and regulatory trends across AI, data governance, and financial systems to position OnCorps as an industry leader.

AI-Enabled Development & Operational Excellence

  • Implement and scale coding agents, testing agents, and AI-assisted development tools across the organization to maximize developer productivity.
  • Establish metrics and observability dashboards to monitor platform performance, CI/CD throughput, deployment frequency, and engineering velocity.
  • Lead the scaling of OnCorps’ SaaS architecture to support a growing client base and increasingly complex use cases.
  • Ensure robust data governance, model transparency, and explainability across all AI-driven products.
  • Build and maintain a secure, scalable, and high-performance platform that meets the rigorous standards of global asset managers and fund administrators.
  • Partner closely with InfoSec on technical risk management, security compliance (SOC 2, GDPR), and infrastructure reliability.

Team Leadership & Engineering Culture

  • Build, mentor, and scale high-performing Engineering and DevOps teams, establishing clear structures, feedback loops, and career progression pathways.
  • Attract, hire, and retain top technical talent specialized in enterprise SaaS, distributed systems, and applied AI applications.
  • Cultivate a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration.

Cross-Functional & Stakeholder Partnership

  • Collaborate with Implementation, Customer Success, and Go-to-Market teams to align engineering output with enterprise reliability, uptime, and client delivery standards.
  • Engage with key enterprise clients and technical stakeholders to understand complex integration requirements, architectural, and data management needs.
  • Partner with the Head of AI to integrate research, innovation, and development of advanced AI capabilities, LLMOps and agentic functionality into the OnCorps platform.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of progressive technical leadership experience, including 5+ years as a VP of Engineering, Director of Engineering, or equivalent in a financial technology or enterprise software company.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field required; advanced technical degree preferred.
  • Proven experience scaling an enterprise-grade technology stack, including cloud infrastructure, operations, DevOps, and CI/CD best practices.
  • Deep understanding of data-intensive systems, machine learning operations (MLOps), and AI-driven agentic applications.
  • Hands-on familiarity with modern technologies such as Python, NodeJS, cloud-native containerized microservices (AWS/Azure/GCP), Kubernetes, and modern data pipelines.
  • Experience designing and managing secure, compliant, and high-availability systems serving institutional clients.
  • Proven success leading distributed teams and fostering engineering excellence in a high-growth, innovation-focused environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and lead an AI-enabled engineering organization, leveraging AI-assisted development tools and workflows to significantly improve engineering velocity and productivity
  • Strategic Technologist: Able to think several steps ahead and translate technology decisions into long-term business value.
  • Hands-On Leader: Balances technical depth with executive communication and decision-making.
  • Collaborative Partner: Works seamlessly across product, client, and commercial functions.
  • Innovator: Excited by the challenge of applying AI and data science to transform legacy processes in capital markets.
  • Operationally Rigorous: Values scalability, reliability, and engineering discipline in equal measure.
  • Mission-Driven: Shares OnCorps’ commitment to transparency, integrity, and responsible AI.
  • Effective Communicator: Able to translate complex concepts, ideas, challenges and solutions between people with differing backgrounds and expertise (e.g. technology, business, customers) to align all parties to common goals and solutions.

Why You Should Join Us

This is a compelling opportunity to define and scale the technology foundation of a category-defining AI company at the forefront of capital markets innovation. You’ll partner directly with the CPTO and executive team to shape product, data, and infrastructure strategy across a growing portfolio of Tier 1 enterprise clients. The position offers a competitive compensation package, comprehensive benefits, and professional development support.

Apply today and be a part of the future of financial services technology!

jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

Mamaya Health is seeking an experienced Accounts Receivable Assistant to join our Revenue Cycle Management team. This role supports the financial health of the organization through accurate claims management, insurance follow-up, denial resolution, payment research, and maintenance of outstanding accounts receivable.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with mental and/or behavioral health billing and understands the full insurance claim lifecycle. This individual should be comfortable independently researching complex claim issues, communicating with insurance carriers, identifying the root cause of denials or underpayments, and taking appropriate action to bring claims to resolution.

The Accounts Receivable Specialist will work closely with the revenue cycle manager and other members of the Mamaya Health team to ensure claims are processed accurately and efficiently while providing professional, compassionate support to clients and staff.

IDEAL CANDIDATE

  • Previous experience in mental and/or behavioral health medical billing.
  • Working knowledge of Commercial, EAP, and Medicaid insurance plans.
  • Strong understanding of primary and secondary insurance billing, including coordination of benefits (COB), claim sequencing, and secondary claim submission.
  • Experience researching and resolving insurance denials, rejections, underpayments, overpayments, and requests for additional information.
  • Knowledge of eligibility, benefits, copays, deductibles, coinsurance, and patient responsibility.
  • Comfort communicating directly with insurance carriers regarding claim status and resolution.
  • Dependable, organized, detail-oriented, adaptable, and able to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, initiative, critical thinking, and problem-solving ability.
  • Ability to work independently while recognizing when an issue should be escalated.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Behavioral or mental health billing experience is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of Commercial, EAP, and Medicaid billing requirements.
  • Experience working insurance Accounts Receivable (AR).
  • Experience with claim submission, corrected claims, reconsiderations, appeals, and denial management.
  • Familiarity with payer portals and electronic claim systems.

• Experience with AdvancedMD preferred.

• Proficiency with Google Workspace.

  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to research complex billing issues through resolution.

JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Work assigned insurance AR queues and maintain accounts within aging expectations established by Revenue Cycle leadership.
  • Investigate claim denials, rejections, edits, underpayments, overpayments, requests for information, and other payer correspondence.
  • Identify root causes of claim issues and take appropriate corrective action.
  • Review claims for billing accuracy and correct errors prior to resubmission.
  • Submit corrected claims, reconsiderations, and appeals when appropriate.
  • Follow up directly with insurance carriers and payer representatives regarding outstanding or incorrectly processed claims.
  • Appropriately process claims involving primary and secondary insurance, including coordination of benefits and claim submission order.
  • Submit or facilitate secondary claims after primary insurance adjudication.
  • Obtain necessary documentation or information from clients, providers, or internal team members to resolve outstanding claims.
  • Assist with obtaining or correcting insurance information when necessary.
  • Document all claim follow-up activity and payer communications clearly and accurately.
  • Generate and maintain reports necessary to ensure assigned AR is actively worked.
  • Identify recurring denial trends or payer issues and communicate findings to Revenue Cycle leadership.
  • Escalate complex or high-risk accounts appropriately and support other Revenue Cycle functions as needed.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

HOURS & LOCATION

  • Part-time position with the potential to transition to full-time based on organizational needs.
  • Monday through Friday; hours to be discussed during interview process
  • This is a remote, work-from-home position.

SUPPORT & EMPOWERMENT

The Accounts Receivable Specialist will work closely with and receive support from Mamaya Health's Revenue Cycle leadership team. We believe strong revenue cycle performance requires collaboration, accountability, clear communication, and giving team members the resources and autonomy necessary to resolve issues effectively.

ABOUT MAMAYA HEALTH

Mamaya Health is committed to creating an environment centered on compassionate, accessible mental healthcare. Our team values collaboration, inclusivity, authenticity, continuous improvement, and providing an exceptional experience for both our clients and our staff.

We are looking for someone who understands the technical side of Revenue Cycle Management and recognizes that every claim represents a client receiving care.

Salary: $24

jobs.description:
The Digital Advertising Manager will lead the strategy, execution, and optimization of digital advertising campaigns across Moonshot's U.S. Online Violence Prevention portfolio. This role combines hands-on digital advertising expertise with strategic campaign oversight, budget management, creative innovation, and technical leadership. Unlike traditional commercial advertising, our campaigns seek to influence awareness, attitudes, and behaviors, including encouraging help-seeking and building resilience to harmful narratives. The successful candidate must understand how to adapt digital marketing strategies, audience engagement approaches, and performance measurement to these objectives, rather than relying solely on traditional conversion metrics.

A key priority is advancing Moonshot's digital campaigning capabilities to incorporate more engaging and innovative approaches, including video, visual storytelling, creator and influencer partnerships, emerging technologies, and other creative formats. Reporting to a Senior Manager, this role will provide project direction to junior campaign managers and serve as the team's primary technical resource, offering hands-on troubleshooting, training, and coaching to strengthen the team's advertising capabilities.

Candidates must be based in MA, CO, NY, VA, GA, PA, MD, WI, TN, TX, OR, NJ, or DC. Occasional travel may be required.

Your responsibilities will include:

Digital Advertising Strategy & Campaign Delivery

  • Lead digital advertising strategy across multiple prevention campaigns, translating intervention objectives into effective audience targeting, channel selection, creative approaches, and campaign plans.
  • Oversee the full campaign lifecycle, from creative development and setup through launch, optimization, and reporting, providing hands-on technical expertise and troubleshooting when needed.
  • Manage advertising budgets across campaigns and platforms, including allocation, pacing, forecasting, and expenditure tracking.
  • Analyze advertising performance and cost-effectiveness, using findings to improve engagement, conversions, targeting, and resource allocation.
  • Maintain relationships with advertising platforms and vendors, staying current on platform capabilities, policies, and emerging practices.

Creative Strategy & Innovation

  • Lead the evolution of Moonshot's digital advertising approaches, expanding beyond predominantly text-based advertising through video, visual storytelling, interactive content, creator and influencer partnerships, and emerging technologies.
  • Develop and test innovative creative formats and audience engagement strategies, using experimentation and performance data to identify and scale effective approaches.
  • Explore emerging technologies and changes in digital discovery, including AI-enabled creative tools and generative engine optimization (GEO).

Technical Leadership & Team Development

  • Provide project direction and technical oversight to junior campaign managers and analysts, ensuring effective day-to-day delivery.
  • Serve as the team's primary technical resource, providing hands-on troubleshooting, training, and coaching to develop colleagues' advertising capabilities.
  • Establish technical standards, quality assurance procedures, and best practices that support consistent, high-quality campaign execution.

Measurement, Insights & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead advertising performance measurement and reporting, establishing meaningful indicators of reach, engagement, conversions, and cost-effectiveness appropriate to campaign objectives.
  • Work with intervention design and evaluation colleagues to ensure advertising metrics contribute to understanding broader prevention outcomes, rather than relying solely on traditional commercial conversion measures.
  • Translate campaign findings into recommendations for improvement, strengthening reporting practices, technical processes, and future campaign methodologies.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Client Engagement

  • Collaborate with intervention specialists, project managers, Product & Engineering colleagues, and external partners to ensure digital strategies support evidence-informed prevention objectives.
  • Brief clients, partners, and funders on advertising strategies, performance, findings, and recommendations, translating technical information into actionable insights.
  • Contribute digital advertising expertise to proposals, project scoping, budgets, and business development opportunities.

Quality Assurance & Ethical Delivery

  • Ensure campaigns meet high standards of technical quality, accuracy, platform compliance, and responsible advertising practice.
  • Identify and mitigate operational, technical, reputational, and safeguarding risks, ensuring alignment with Moonshot's ethical standards and applicable privacy requirements.

Requirements

Essential:

  • Demonstrated experience developing, managing, and optimizing digital advertising campaigns, including strategic responsibility for multiple campaigns and advertising budgets.
  • Hands-on expertise with major digital advertising platforms, including campaign setup, troubleshooting, optimization, audience targeting, A/B testing, and performance measurement.
  • Experience with non-commercial campaigns, such as strategic communications, public health, or social impact, or demonstrated ability to adapt commercial digital advertising approaches to awareness, behavior change, and other non-transactional objectives.
  • Experience developing innovative advertising strategies, creative formats, and audience engagement approaches, using performance data to inform improvements.
  • Strong analytical, budgeting, and project management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities and optimize advertising expenditure.
  • Experience providing technical guidance, coaching, or training to colleagues, particularly less experienced campaign staff.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts for non-specialist stakeholders.
  • Candidates must be eligible to work in the US, and will be required to undertake and pass any relevant security clearance procedures per client needs.

Desirable:

  • Experience with video advertising, visual storytelling, creator or influencer marketing, interactive content, or other innovative digital engagement formats.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled creative technologies, generative engine optimization (GEO), or emerging digital discovery approaches.
  • Experience working in a digital marketing agency, consultancy, or other multi-client environment.
  • Knowledge of targeted violence prevention, P/CVE, online harms, or related fields.
  • Experience developing standardized advertising processes, training resources, or technical quality assurance frameworks.

Benefits

Parexel is a leading global clinical development partner delivering insights-driven clinical and consulting solutions to the life sciences industry. With 22,000+ employees worldwide, we partner with biopharmaceutical companies and research sites to design and deliver patient-focused clinical trials that broaden access and make research a care option for anyone, anywhere.


We work with focus, agility, and shared purpose, moving with urgency to address patient needs and accelerate the delivery of new therapies. As an Associate Clinical Operations Leader, you will take on Clinical Operations Leader responsibilities for assigned countries or selected tasks, supporting clinical research activities that advance new treatments for patients. This position plays a key role in study execution, ICH-GCP and regulatory compliance, and clinical data quality. You will work under the guidance of an experienced Clinical Operations Leader, collaborate with cross-functional teams, follow industry-standard processes, and contribute to study operations from start-up through close-out.

This role may also be part of a global project management team.

  • Support process improvement initiatives and contribute lessons learned at study close-out

jobs.description:
Job Description

Goucher College’s Graduate & Professional Studies seeks non-tenure-track adjunct faculty to teach the following graduate courses within the M.A. in Policy Analytics (MAPA) program. The course will be offered synchronously online (via Microsoft Teams), starting on January 25, 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates who can deepen our students’ understanding of the interactions between the practical use of analytical tools and methods for evaluating, designing, and improving public policies. Contracts for adjunct faculty are subject to renewal on a semester-by-semester basis, depending on factors such as enrollment, instructor availability and performance, and student success.

Course Description: Social Problems and Public Policy Making (3 credits)

Social Problems and Public Policy-Making offers a critical examination of the relationship between social policy and social justice in the United States. The course explores the tension between universal and population-specific approaches to welfare provision and their implications for equity and inclusion. Students will analyze contemporary policy domains—including health care, economic inequality, racial justice, gender equity, and environmental justice—while situating them within broader processes of social, economic, and cultural developments. Students will develop and apply theoretical and empirical tools for analyzing political and ideological conflicts over social issues and their effect on policymaking.

Responsibilities

• Teach all scheduled weekly sessions using the approved course description and learning outcomes.

• Develop or adapt a syllabus, readings, assignments and rubrics.

• Lead seminar-style discussion and critical analysis of policy cases, e.g. in health care, economic inequality, racial justice, gender equity and environmental justice.

• Teach students to apply theoretical frameworks and empirical evidence to policy debates, including universal versus targeted approaches to welfare provision.

• Guide students through applied work such as policy briefs, stakeholder analyses or research papers.

• Foster an inclusive classroom where students engage respectfully across differing political and ideological views.

• Give timely, substantive feedback and submit final grades by university deadlines.

• Hold regular office hours (virtual) and respond to student messages within 48 hours.

• Maintain course materials and grades in the learning management system Canvas.

• Follow university policies on academic integrity, accessibility accommodations and FERPA.

Requirements:

A successful candidate would be able to begin teaching on January 25, 2027, and teach the course on Tuesday or Wednesday evenings. Preference is given to candidates who have previously taught such a course and/or have substantial professional policy expertise.

Required Qualifications:

  • A Master’s degree or Ph.D. in a relevant field, such as public policy, political science, public administration, sociology, or a closely related field.
  • Candidates with a master's degree and applicable work experience are highly encouraged to apply.
  • Subject-matter expertise in U.S. social policy and at least one of the course's policy domains required.
  • Commitment to equity, inclusion and respectful engagement with diverse perspectives in the classroom.
  • Comfortable working with students from diverse disciplinary and professional backgrounds, including those without strong math or coding foundations and guide them through individual projects and team-based work.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills.
  • At least one year of experience teaching at the college level, M.A. level preferred.

Preferred Qualifications/Experience:

  • Professional experience in policymaking, advocacy, government, nonprofit or community organizations.
  • A record of research or applied work on topics such as health policy, poverty and inequality, racial or gender equity, or environmental justice.
  • Skill with both qualitative and quantitative methods for policy analysis.
  • Experience with online or hybrid teaching and active-learning techniques.

Salary: $1,260-$1,443 per credit

(dependent on OR commensurate with experience)

Application Instruction: Interested candidates should submit the following materials:

  • A curriculum vitae
  • A cover letter that contextualizes the candidate’s teaching experience, subject interests, and professional experience.
  • Sample syllabus and teaching evaluations, if available.
  • Contact information for two references. Recommendation will be solicited if selected for an interview.

The review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled.  

For questions, contact Stefanie I. Kasparek ().


Applicants must reside in: Colorado, Delaware, District of Columbia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Texas, and Virginia.

AECOM is seeking an experienced Secure Facilities Technical Engineering - Mission Critical & Secure Facilities to support our national Mission Critical and Secure Facilities practice, providing technical leadership for the design and execution of secure and classified facilities for U.S. federal, Department of War, and Intelligence Community clients.

This role is focused on the technical implementation of ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, Open Storage Secret (OSS), TEMPEST, and related security requirements, translating security criteria into coordinated, constructible architectural and engineering solutions, construction documents, specifications, and technical details.

The successful candidate will serve as a technical liaison between government security stakeholders and multidisciplinary project teams and possess a strong understanding of how physical and technical security requirements integrate with architectural, engineering, telecommunications, audiovisual, electronic security, and other building systems. The position will support projects throughout both CONUS and OCONUS locations.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Serve as a technical lead for secure facility design and execution, interpreting and applying ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, OSS, TEMPEST, and related physical and technical security criteria.
  • Translate security requirements into coordinated design criteria, construction documents, specifications, technical details, and constructible solutions.
  • Lead multidisciplinary coordination with architects, engineers, technology and security specialists, contractors, and government stakeholders, including SSMs, SSOs, CTTAs, and Accrediting Officials.
  • Develop and review technical solutions for secure perimeter construction, doors and openings, penetrations, acoustic protection, access control, intrusion detection, and other physical security requirements.
  • Coordinate TEMPEST and RF mitigation strategies, including RF shielding, non-conductive breaks, waveguide-below-cutoff penetrations, power and signal filtering, grounding/bonding, and related countermeasures.
  • Conduct existing-condition surveys, facility assessments, and feasibility studies for new construction, renovation, conversion, and upgrade of secure environments.
  • Perform technical design, interdisciplinary coordination, quality-control, and constructability reviews to ensure security requirements are appropriately incorporated into project documentation.
  • Provide technical support during construction, including review of submittals, RFIs, shop drawings, field conditions, inspections, testing, and resolution of security-related issues, and support accreditation/certification and project closeout as applicable.
  • Support development and implementation of secure facility standards, specifications, details, tools, and best practices, while maintaining awareness of evolving government security criteria.
  • Support proposal development, technical approaches, scopes of work, and strategic growth opportunities for the Mission Critical and Secure Facilities practice.

Successful candidates will demonstrate the following critical qualifications and capabilities:

  • Demonstrated experience interpreting and implementing ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, OSS, TEMPEST, and related secure facility requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate security requirements into construction drawings, specifications, technical details, and multidisciplinary design solutions.
  • Knowledge of secure perimeter construction and RF/TEMPEST mitigation techniques, including penetrations, shielding, non-conductive breaks, waveguide-below-cutoff protection, and power/signal filtering.
  • Strong understanding of multidisciplinary building systems and their interaction with physical and technical security requirements.
  • Experience with secure facility assessments, technical design reviews, and construction-phase support.
  • Strong technical leadership, coordination, written communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability and willingness to travel periodically in support of CONUS and OCONUS projects.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related building design or technical discipline and 10+ years including two years of leadership, of professional experience, including significant experience with federal secure, classified, or mission-critical facilities or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
  • Professional registration appropriate to the candidate's discipline, such as Registered Architect (RA), or comparable professional credential.
  • Ability to pass drug, and background checks to work on Federal grounds, military installations, and school grounds.
  • This position requires U.S. citizenship due to federal contract/security requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 15+ years of professional experience, including 5+ years focused on SCIF, SAPF, TEMPEST, OSS, or comparable secure/classified facilities.
  • Advanced experience with the design, documentation, construction, inspection, and accreditation/certification of secure facilities.
  • Completion of recognized training related to ICD 705, SCIF/SAPF design and construction, TEMPEST, RF shielding, or related secure facility criteria.
  • Experience working directly with SSMs, SSOs, CTTAs, Accrediting Officials, and other government security authorities.
  • Experience developing secure facility standards, specifications, standard details, design guides, or quality-control procedures.
  • Experience supporting secure facility projects in both CONUS and OCONUS locations.

Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Director, Marketing AI & GTM Automation, you will be tasked with building and leading a marketing-led team that owns how AI and automation are applied across the go-to-market motion. you will set the AI strategy for marketing's GTM work, decide which use cases get built and in what order, ship the systems that transform how teams execute, and run those systems as durable, measured infrastructure. this role owns the full arc of strategy, implementation, and run-the-business work, partnering daily with demand generation, PLG, SDR, product marketing, brand, and marketing operations, as well as revenue operations, revenue technology, sales, IT/security, and legal..

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • AI use-case roadmap: Maintain a prioritized, revenue-linked backlog of AI and automation use cases across the GTM funnel. Translate operational friction ("our lead response is too slow," "campaign QA is manual") into scoped, sequenced initiatives with defined success metrics, rather than chasing tool novelty.
  • Governance and trust: Own the marketing-specific guardrails for AI, including what systems are permitted to do on the brand's behalf, what data they can access, which outputs require human review, and how everything is logged and audited. Coordinate with legal, security, and compliance on policy and risk.
  • The marketing technology stack and its AI layer: Own the architecture, integration layer, and roadmap for the marketing tech stack (marketing automation, CDP, orchestration, analytics, and the marketing side of CRM) and the AI layer that now sits across it. Partner with revenue technology and sales-systems owners where workflows cross team lines, rather than absorbing their scope. Manage vendor selection, contracts, and consolidation; prevent tool sprawl.
  • Implementation and delivery: Set standards for how AI agents and agentic workflows are designed, built, evaluated, and deployed. Own the evaluation discipline, including output quality scoring, benchmarking, and regression testing, so that "it works" is measured, not asserted.
  • Enablement and adoption: Build the skill libraries, prompt libraries, training, and coaching motion that get the broader marketing org self-sufficient. Adoption is a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought.
  • Team and craft: Hire, develop, and lead a small team of specialists (GTM engineers, a marketing technology/ops lead, an enablement/governance lead). Set the technical bar, run the operating cadence, and create the career paths that keep scarce talent.
  • Measurement: Define and report the metrics that prove the function's value, including cycle-time reduction, output quality, cost-to-serve, and pipeline and revenue influence, to the CMO and cross-functional leadership.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 8+ years across marketing/GTM operations, marketing technology, growth, or a related function, with meaningful time owning systems that directly touched pipeline or revenue
  • 3+ years leading and developing people, ideally a mix of technical and operational talent
  • Demonstrated ownership of a modern GTM/marketing tech stack, including Salesforce, Marketo, CDP platforms (Segment, Tealium, mParticle, Adobe Real-Time CDP), and analytics/orchestration tools (Snowflake, Looker, Tableau, Adobe Experience Platform)
  • Hands-on fluency with how AI is built into GTM work today, including agent frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex), LLM platforms (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini), evaluation/observability tools (LangSmith, Braintrust), and human-in-the-loop review and prompt architecture practices
  • A track record of translating strategy into shipped systems, and of driving adoption across teams you don't directly manage
  • Strong cross-functional judgment, comfortable partnering with legal, security, sales, and product to ship safely
  • Preferred: Experience standing up or scaling an AI/automation function inside a larger marketing or broader GTM organization
  • Preferred: Familiarity with agent frameworks, orchestration platforms (e.g., n8n, Make), APIs/MCP integrations, and lightweight scripting (SQL, Python, or JavaScript), enough to be dangerous, not necessarily to build production code yourself
  • Preferred: B2B / enterprise SaaS background
  • Preferred: Experience building measurement and governance frameworks for AI in a regulated or brand-sensitive environment

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.
