jobs.description:
Talent Acquisition Administrator

The Talent Acquisition Administrator provides administrative and systems support to the Talent Acquisition team, reporting to the Director, Talent Acquisition. This role owns the day-to-day upkeep of the applicant tracking system (ATS), keeps job requisitions accurate and current, and helps process employee job changes, including promotions, demotions, and transfers. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable working with confidential information across HR systems.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Maintain the applicant tracking system (ATS), including user access, job templates, workflows, candidate statuses, and system settings, in partnership with the Director, Talent Acquisition
  • Audit open, on-hold, and filled requisitions on a regular cadence to ensure accurate status, approvals, hiring manager, recruiter assignment, and position details
  • Open, update, and close job requisitions in the ATS according to approval workflows, and resolve duplicate, stale, or incomplete requisitions
  • Reconcile ATS requisition data against HRIS and headcount/position records and flag discrepancies to Talent Acquisition and HR leadership
  • Assist in processing employee job changes, including promotions, demotions, lateral moves, and transfers, by preparing documentation, routing approvals, and entering changes accurately and on time
  • Coordinate with HR, Payroll, and hiring managers to confirm effective dates, compensation changes, and required paperwork for job changes
  • Generate recurring and ad hoc ATS and requisition reports (e.g., open requisitions, time-to-fill, pipeline status) for the Talent Acquisition team and leadership
  • Serve as a first point of contact for recruiter and hiring manager ATS questions; provide basic troubleshooting and training, and escalate system issues to the vendor as needed
  • Maintain and document ATS and requisition procedures, data standards, and job aids
  • Maintain confidentiality of candidate and employee information and ensure records comply with company policy and applicable recordkeeping requirements
  • Understand and demonstrate safe work practices at all times to ensure a safe work environment
  • Comply with all company policies and procedures
  • Complete special projects and other duties as assigned by your supervisor

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data entry, auditing, and recordkeeping
  • Working knowledge of applicant tracking systems and HR information systems, with the ability to learn new platforms quickly
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel (sorting, filtering, lookups, and basic reporting)
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with a customer-service mindset when supporting recruiters and hiring managers
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion
  • Basic understanding of HR processes such as requisition approvals, job changes, and employee data management

Experience and Credentials

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred
  • 1–3 years of experience in an HR, recruiting, or administrative support role
  • Hands-on experience using an applicant tracking system (e.g., Workday, iCIMS, Greenhouse, SuccessFactors, or similar) required. Experience in ADP Recruitment Manager and ADP Lyric highly preferred.
  • Experience processing employee data changes in an HRIS preferred

Physical & Work Environment Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Ability to travel occasionally for meetings, training, or customer engagements.
  • Must be able to communicate effectively in person, over the phone, and via digital platforms.

jobs.excerpt: Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) $62K-80K/yr Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further!
jobs.description:
Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) $62K-80K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $62,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LPC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. About us

Itero Group is a Women-Owned Small Business focused on simplifying complex transformations. Itero Group is seeking an experienced, hands-on Scrum Master II to support a software development team within a large-scale federal healthcare program. The ideal candidate will bring a practical understanding of Agile methodologies, strong facilitation and delivery coordination skills, and the ability to support a technical team operating within established sprint cycles and quarterly release schedules.

This role requires someone who understands how to apply Agile principles to drive results rather than simply following processes. The Scrum Master will work closely with developers, business analysts, technical leadership, and the Product Owner to remove impediments, maintain delivery momentum, and promote continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives, and backlog refinement.

  • Support a cross-functional software development team operating in three-week sprints with quarterly release commitments.

  • Identify and remove impediments, manage dependencies, and help ensure sprint goals and delivery milestones are achieved.

  • Partner with the Product Owner, technical lead, developers, and business analysts to coordinate priorities, activities, and deliverables.

  • Track sprint progress, risks, dependencies, and team performance using Jira dashboards, metrics, and reporting tools.

  • Coordinate system demonstrations, including preparation, stakeholder communication, and execution.

  • Analyze Agile metrics and identify opportunities to improve team productivity, accountability, and delivery performance.

  • Support project coordination, status reporting, and administrative activities to maintain visibility into team progress.

  • Apply Agile and Scaled Agile practices within a structured delivery environment, balancing flexibility with established release requirements.

  • Collaborate with other Scrum Masters and PMO leadership to establish consistent Agile practices, reporting standards, and delivery processes.

  • Promote team collaboration, ownership, continuous improvement, and effective communication across technical and business stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience serving as a Scrum Master supporting software development teams in an Agile environment.

  • Strong working knowledge of Scrum, Agile methodologies, and Scaled Agile concepts.

  • Experience supporting teams operating within fixed release schedules, enterprise delivery environments, or hybrid Agile frameworks.

  • Proven ability to facilitate Agile ceremonies, remove obstacles, and support successful sprint execution.

  • Hands-on experience with Jira, including sprint tracking, backlog management, dashboards, metrics, and reporting.

  • Experience analyzing team performance metrics, identifying delivery risks, and communicating progress to stakeholders.

  • Strong organizational, facilitation, problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively with technical and business teams.

  • Practical, results-oriented approach to Agile delivery with the ability to adapt processes to meet team and program needs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting federal government or healthcare technology programs.

  • Familiarity with CMS, Medicare, healthcare claims processing, or medical policy systems.

  • Experience supporting mainframe, legacy application development, or enterprise modernization initiatives.

  • Exposure to batch processing systems and complex enterprise application environments.

  • Experience working within a Project Management Office (PMO) or supporting Agile process standardization across multiple teams.

  • Background in project coordination, delivery reporting, or traditional project management activities.

Technical Environment

The Scrum Master will support a software development team responsible for enterprise applications and legacy systems within a federal healthcare environment. The team operates in three-week sprint cycles with established quarterly releases.

While deep technical development or mainframe expertise is not required, candidates should be comfortable collaborating with technical teams, understanding development activities at a high level, identifying dependencies, and coordinating delivery timelines.

Agile certifications are not required. Relevant hands-on experience, sound judgment, adaptability, and demonstrated success supporting software delivery are the primary considerations.

About Itero Group

Itero Group is a women-owned small business focused on delivering innovative technology solutions and consulting services to commercial and government clients. We are committed to providing exceptional service, fostering collaboration, and helping our clients achieve meaningful business outcomes.

Itero Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants.

If you are looking for a role where you will lead with integrity, create and innovate, inspire excellence, be a respected member of the team, drive results, and have fun, we look forward to connecting with you!

Benefits at Itero Group
At Itero Group, we’re proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance:

  • Health & Wellness: Medical (BC-BS), dental, and vision plans to suit your needs.
  • Paid Time Off: Generous PTO, paid holidays, and increasing PTO based on years of service.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with company match and auto-enrollment.
  • Company-Paid Coverage: Short-term and long-term disability, life insurance, and AD&D insurance.
  • Additional Options: Voluntary benefits including pet insurance and student loan assistance up to $1,000 annually.
  • Perks: FSAs, HSAs, wellness programs, and more to enhance your work-life balance.

Join us and enjoy a benefits package designed with you in mind!

This role is ideal for an engineer who is passionate about modern data architecture, cloud-native infrastructure, and mentoring others while delivering high-impact systems that make data a true asset.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as a senior technical contributor helping shape the design of scalable, modular, and performant data systems.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to design and deliver reliable data pipelines for analytics, reporting, and data science use cases.
  • Develop and optimize ELT workflows using modern tools such as Airbyte, Fivetran, dbt, and Python.
  • Design and maintain performant data models in Snowflake, including star schemas and other dimensional modeling techniques that support clean, well-structured, and easily consumable datasets - including those optimized for AI tools and text-to-SQL interfaces.
  • Lead efforts to improve data observability, including proactive alerting, monitoring, and incident response capabilities.
  • Explore and implement open table formats (e.g., Apache Iceberg) to enable flexibility, scalability, and interoperability across data systems.
  • Collaborate with DevOps and Cloud teams to ensure our AWS-based infrastructure is optimized for performance, cost, and reliability.
  • Establish and maintain engineering best practices, including version control, code reviews, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing.
  • Act as a mentor to other engineers and analytics professionals, fostering knowledge sharing and high standards for quality and consistency.
  • Stay current on emerging technologies and bring forward recommendations for improving platform capabilities, performance, or efficiency.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • 8+ years in data engineering, architecture, or related technical roles working with large-scale data systems.
  • Deep experience with SQL and Python for data transformation and automation.
  • Hands-on experience with modern data stack tools such as dbt, Airbyte, Fivetran, and Snowflake.
  • Strong understanding of cloud technologies, particularly AWS (e.g., S3, Lambda, EC2, IAM).
  • Familiarity with open data formats and scalable data lakehouse principles (e.g., Iceberg or similar).
  • Experience building and operating workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow.
  • Knowledge of observability and monitoring frameworks to support data platform health and alerting.
  • Comfortable working in Git-based environments with strong CI/CD practices.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor, coach, and collaborate across a multidisciplinary data team.

Compensation

Annual base salary range: $155,000-$165,000, depending on experience and qualifications. This role is also eligible for a variable annual bonus based on both company and individual performance.

Location

All Evolve team members must live in one of our approved locations by their first day. We can hire from anywhere in the U.S. except D.C. and Hawaii. Some positions may also have restrictions based on compensation in the following states: California, Maryland, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, and Washington. If you live in Colorado, you can work remotely anywhere in the state, at our downtown Denver office, or a hybrid of both! If you're planning to move soon, please let us know, and we'll be happy to review your application again.

California Applicant Privacy Policy | Evolve

How we reward Evolvers

We’re intentional about offering benefits that empower every Evolver to thrive both professionally and personally because they’re more than perks—they’re investments in our customer-obsessed, high-performing team.

We believe in treating others as they want to be treated, providing benefits that deliver real value, and challenging the status quo to meet the diverse needs of our team. Whether it’s helping you take care of your health, plan for the future, or celebrate life’s milestones, our offerings are designed to support you every step of the way.

jobs.excerpt: Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs.
jobs.description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values – be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable – creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity

The Senior Director, Clinical Pharmacology is a highly experienced clinical pharmacologist who will provide strategic scientific leadership across multiple development programs from Phase 1 through Phase 3. Reporting to the Vice President, Clinical Pharmacology, this individual will partner with cross-functional program teams to develop and execute clinical pharmacology strategies that support regulatory submissions and successful drug development.

This role will contribute deep expertise in pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), exposure-response analyses, modeling and simulation, and clinical pharmacology study design. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with Clinical Development, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Translational Medicine, Nonclinical, Medical Writing, and external partners to ensure robust clinical pharmacology strategies throughout development.

As an experienced scientific leader, this individual will independently lead assigned programs while collaborating closely with the Vice President and other members of the Clinical Pharmacology team.

We anticipate hiring the Senior Director, Clinical Pharmacology in September 2026

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the Clinical Pharmacology lead for assigned development programs from first-in-human studies through Phase 3 clinical trials.
  • Develop and execute program-specific clinical pharmacology strategies aligned with overall development objectives.
  • Provide scientific leadership for PK, PD, exposure-response, population PK, modeling and simulation activities.
  • Design and oversee clinical pharmacology studies, including protocol development, analysis plans, interpretation of results, and reporting.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate clinical pharmacology into broader development strategies.
  • Partner with Clinical Development physicians, statisticians, pharmacometricians, Regulatory Affairs, Biometrics, and Medical Writing to support program execution.
  • Interpret clinical pharmacology data and translate findings into clear scientific and regulatory recommendations.
  • Contribute to dose selection, dose optimization, labeling strategy, and benefit-risk assessments.
  • Support preparation of regulatory submission documents including INDs, briefing books, CTDs, clinical pharmacology summaries, and responses to health authority questions.
  • Participate in regulatory agency meetings as a clinical pharmacology subject matter expert.
  • Manage external CROs, consultants, and pharmacometric vendors supporting assigned programs.
  • Stay current on emerging clinical pharmacology methodologies, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute to scientific publications, presentations, and internal knowledge sharing.
  • Mentor junior scientists and provide technical guidance across project teams as appropriate.

Required Qualifications

  • PhD, PharmD, MD, or equivalent advanced degree in Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacometrics, or a related scientific discipline.
  • Approximately 10–15+ years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry experience, including significant experience supporting clinical drug development.
  • At least 10 years of direct experience in Clinical Pharmacology.
  • Experience supporting multiple clinical development stages, including early and late-stage development.
  • Experience with biologics, peptides, small molecules, or gene therapies is desirable.
  • Experience preparing regulatory submissions and interacting with FDA and other global health authorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong understanding of PK/PD principles and clinical pharmacology strategy.
  • Experience with population PK and exposure-response analyses.
  • Familiarity with pharmacometric modeling and simulation approaches.
  • Working knowledge of NONMEM, Phoenix WinNonlin, R, SAS, or comparable clinical pharmacology software.
  • Excellent scientific writing and presentation skills.
  • Ability to independently interpret complex clinical data and communicate recommendations to senior leadership.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Demonstrated success working in highly collaborative, cross-functional environments.
  • Ability to manage multiple programs simultaneously in a fast-paced biotechnology environment.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a willingness to contribute broadly across development programs.

Work Location and Conditions

  • At Amylyx, we proudly support remote work opportunities within the United States. However, due to business considerations related to health insurance coverage and state tax regulations, we are unable to hire employees who reside and/or work in certain states. Currently, we are not considering applicants from Alaska, Arizona, Hawaii, Michigan and Tennessee.
  • You will be expected to travel to our corporate location in Cambridge, MA several times a year and attend other company-related events as necessary and requested.
  • You must have access to work in setting which enables meeting all requirements of the role (including privacy, reliable internet access, phone, ability to video conference, etc.) at your remote location.

Compensation

The pay range posted below represents our good faith estimate of compensation for this role, based on market data and internal benchmarks. The final offer may vary depending on a candidate’s experience, skills, and qualifications, as well as considerations of internal equity.

Estimated Pay Range
$268,000—$302,000 USD

Job Summary:

The Program Director of the Doctor of Education in Artificial Intelligence and Moral Agency must be able to lead with expertise in ethics and or Artificial Intelligence with a grounding in Theological Studies. Reporting to the Dean of the Divinity School, The Program Director provides academic leadership and day-to-day administrative oversight for the EdD in Artificial Intelligence and Moral Agency, SUDS's first doctoral-level offering. This person sets the academic vision for the program in partnership with the Dean, ensures the curriculum (theological ethics foundations in Year 1, AI applications and human agency in Year 2, research methods and colloquy in Year 3, and dissertation research in Year 4) is delivered with rigor, and personally teaches, advises, and chairs dissertations within a cohort model designed for bi-vocational adult learners.

Because this is a launch-phase program, the Director will also help build the infrastructure, faculty bench, and external partnerships (e.g., with AI-ethics centers and technical institutions) that the degree will depend on for the next several admissions cycles.

Essential Job Functions:

• Provide overall academic leadership for the EdD program, including curriculum oversight,
learning outcomes, and program review in coordination with the Dean and institutional

accreditation requirements.

• Recruit, mentor, and evaluate full-time and adjunct faculty teaching in the program; build a
roster of instructors with combined strength in theological ethics and AI literacy.
• Teach assigned doctoral seminars and chair or serve on dissertation committees.
• Oversee admissions review for the program in partnership with the Admissions Office, applying
the program's criteria (graduate theological degree, five years of bi-vocational leadership
experience, GPA/equivalency standards).
• Coordinate the three-year residency sequence and annual cohort colloquy, including scheduling,
faculty assignments, and student progress tracking toward the 45-credit (36 coursework plus 9
dissertation) requirement.
• Serve as the primary point of contact for prospective students, partner institutions, and
accreditation bodies regarding the EdD program.
• Develop and manage the program budget, including faculty contracts, library/AI-tool licensing,
and conference or professional-development support for faculty and students.
• Build and maintain relationships with AI-ethics research centers, technology partners, and
continuing-education providers (e.g., for faculty AI-ethics certification) to keep curriculum
current.
• Represent the program at conferences, denominational meetings, and academic associations
relevant to theological education and AI ethics.

• Other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities

FT Faculty, PT-Adjunct Faculty

Minimum Job Qualifications

Required
• Earned doctorate (PhD, ThD, EdD, or DMin) in theology, religious studies, Christian ethics, or a

closely related field.

• A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in theological or graduate
higher education, including teaching at the graduate level.
• Demonstrated experience advising, mentoring, or chairing graduate-level research or
dissertations.
• Working knowledge of core AI ethics concepts and frameworks (e.g., algorithmic fairness, bias
and discrimination, accountability and transparency standards such as the NIST AI Risk
Management Framework) sufficient to guide curriculum and faculty hiring, or a documented
plan to acquire this through certificate study.

the needs of adult professional learners.

sustaining a new doctoral program.

Preferred

  • A practical theologian with professional experience outside a formal religious setting (e.g., healthcare, education, criminal justice, technology, public policy, or nonprofit leadership) that informs an applied, interdisciplinary approach to AI ethics.
  • Record of scholarly publication or conference presentation in theological ethics, AI ethics, or a related interdisciplinary field (e.g., in venues such as Journal of Religion and Health, AI and Ethics, Journal of Moral Theology, or at conferences such as AIES or FAccT).

  • Experience with online or hybrid doctoral program delivery and learning-management systems.

Must have a philosophy that is consistent with the Mission, Vision and Core Values of the
organization. Vision, commitment, and experience in achieving goals and pursuing excellence is
critical: ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic and demanding
environment. Must have strong verbal and written communication and organizational skills; proven
ability to manage multiple complex assignments with sensitivity to deadlines, priorities, and
changing circumstances; demonstrated professional work ethic and positive, problem-solving
attitude. Must be able to read, write and speak fluently in English.

Physical Demands

jobs.description:
Seed Health is a microbiome science company pioneering clinically validated innovations for gut and whole-body health.Our portfolio of gut-directed products is developed in collaboration with leading scientists and backed by human clinical research. We’ve since expanded our offerings to include PDS-08® for pediatric health, VS-01™ for vaginal health, and a new category of Co-Biotics for daily nutrition, energy, and sleep—each grounded in our commitment to scientific rigor, precision formulation, and impact across the body’s interconnected systems. Beyond the body, SeedLabs—our environmental research division—advances microbial solutions that restore biodiversity and support ecosystems affected by human activity.

We’ve built a profitable DTC business with category-leading retention, grown revenue 5x in the last 36 months, and expanded our reach across new channels and markets. With a robust clinical pipeline and continued expansion into new areas of microbiome health, we’re building for scale—with integrity, care, and curiosity.

Our work has been recognized by Fast Company (Most Innovative Companies, Brands That Matter, World Changing Ideas), TIME (Best Inventions), Forbes (America’s Best Startup Employers), and Inc. (Best in Business, Female Founder 100)—a reflection of the science behind our products and the stories we tell to bring them into the world.

We’re a galaxy-class team of researchers, clinicians, designers, engineers, storytellers, and builders—each aligned in our belief in the transformative potential of the microbiome. If you’re a kindred dot-connector looking to shape the future of health, join us.

  • • •

You

You are the technical owner of the systems that run Seed's business behind the scenes. Reporting into our Technology team and partnering daily with Finance and Accounting & Operations, you'll architect, build, govern and support our ERP ecosystem—NetSuite at the core, connected to Shopify/Recharge, 3PL (fulfillment), Ramp (spend management), EDI and more. This is a deeply hands-on role: you write the SuiteScript, design the integrations, and own the governance that keeps a high-volume, multi-channel, multi-entity business running cleanly at scale. You're also an AI-native builder—you see agentic workflows, LLMs, and tools like Claude and MCP not as novelties but as core infrastructure for the next generation of finance and operations systems, and you'll help lead Seed's adoption of them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Consult with business units across Finance, Operations, Growth, and Tech to gather requirements, translate business needs into ERP solutions, and prioritize a systems roadmap that serves the whole company
  • Own the architecture, administration, and development of NetSuite as Seed's system of record across multiple sales channels (DTC, Amazon, & Retail)
  • Design, build, and maintain SuiteScript solutions (Map/Reduce, Scheduled, User Event, RESTlets), workflows, saved searches, and SuiteQL-driven automation
  • Own the integration layer end to end—flows, 3PL transactions, Ramp, and other platforms —including monitoring, error handling, and recovery
  • Establish and enforce systems governance: script deployment standards, sandbox and release management, API concurrency and governance-limit management, change control, and documentation
  • Build AI-augmented workflows using LLMs, MCP connectors, and agentic tooling to automate reconciliation, billing operations, reporting, and cross-system data quality—and champion AI-native practices across the systems function
  • Partner with the Controller and accounting team on close automation, billing remediation, revenue data integrity, and audit-readiness of system controls
  • Design user-friendly interfaces and functionality—custom forms, roles, dashboards, and saved searches—so non-technical teams can self-serve confidently
  • Provide training, support, and enablement for end-users, and prepare technical documentation and training manuals that make our systems knowledge durable rather than tribal
  • Manage systems projects end to end—scoping, timelines, implementation partners, and consultants—and own budgeting and forecasting for the ERP/SaaS stack, evaluating and integrating new tools as it evolves
  • Serve as escalation point for systems incidents, performing diagnostic testing and root-cause analysis and building durable fixes rather than patches

Who You Are:

  • 7+ years in ERP/business systems roles, including 5+ years of hands-on NetSuite administration and development in a multi-entity environment
  • Expert in SuiteScript 2.x, SuiteQL, NetSuite REST/SuiteTalk APIs, and Token-Based Authentication; you've built and debugged production Map/Reduce scripts and RESTlets, not just configured workflows
  • Deep experience with iPaaS platforms (Celigo strongly preferred) and high-volume integration patterns, including concurrency management and error recovery
  • Experienced in DTC/subscription commerce or omnichannel consumer businesses, where order volumes are measured in the hundreds of thousands
  • Integration Management: Configure and support EDI connections (such as EDI 850, 810, 856) between NetSuite and third-party systems or VAN providers.

  • A skilled project manager with experience owning software budgets, forecasting systems spend, and delivering cross-functional implementations on time
  • An exceptional communicator and translator—you make complex technical concepts legible to business stakeholders, and business needs precise for technical execution
  • An analytical problem-solver with strong business acumen; a natural collaborator who leads and mentors others (specialists, consultants, and power users) even without formal reports
  • Highly organized and rigorous about governance and documentation; you know that at scale, undisciplined systems fail loudly and expensively

Licensed Mental Health Professional (LCSW/LMFT/LPC/LMHC) 62K-80K/yr

FLSA Status: Exempt

Salary:

62K - 80K+

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $62,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LMHC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. Seed is seeking a Senior Product Manager (Member Product), reporting to the VP, Digital Product + Ecommerce, to own the end-to-end post-purchase member experience—from the moment a member converts through ongoing retention, cross-sell, and deepening engagement. As Seed expands into retail, Amazon, and new marketplaces, the member experience becomes the connective tissue across channels; this role defines what that experience should become and proves it in the market through rapid experimentation.

  • Own the end-to-end post-purchase member experience strategy, defining what Seed’s member journey should look and feel like, how it evolves, and what to build to make it real.
  • Translate Seed’s science, brand, and retention goals into a clear product vision that earns sustained member engagement.
  • Design and run short-cycle experiments that test strategic hypotheses about member behavior and generate real signal.
  • Define the membership value architecture, grounded in what members want and what moves retention.
  • Own the content delivery strategy that makes science education a retention driver, moving toward dynamic, personalized surfacing.
  • Partner with Product Design to set the creative and strategic direction for member-facing experiences, including the member homepage and subscription management.
  • Collaborate with Growth Product on the funnel-to-member handoff and cross-sell positioning within the member journey.
  • Contribute to multi-category expansion by understanding how multi-product subscription behaviors develop and where the experience must evolve.
  • Inform how Seed’s owned digital experience evolves alongside emerging agentic commerce channels.
  • Define how Seed’s owned member experience works alongside retail, Amazon, and marketplace channels, giving customers who first find Seed elsewhere a reason to become direct members and keeping the experience consistent wherever members buy.
  • Produce a data-grounded product roadmap informed by audience segmentation and multi-product cohort data.
  • Present member experience strategy and experiment results to leadership.
  • And other ad-hoc responsibilities and projects from time to time based on business needs.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within 6 months: a clear, defensible member experience strategy, and at least two experiments launched and generating real signal.

  • Within 12 months: a recommendation on membership tier architecture backed by in-market data.
  • Within 12 months: a content delivery system that has moved beyond static logic toward dynamic, personalized surfacing.

jobs.title: Director of Employee Health and Safety
jobs.excerpt: The START Center for Cancer Research (“START”) is the world’s largest early phase site network, fully dedicated to oncology clinical research.
jobs.description:
The START Center for Cancer Research (“START”) is the world’s largest early phase site network, fully dedicated to oncology clinical research. To date, over 45 therapies conducted at START locations have obtained FDA/EMA approval.

The START Center for Cancer Research is seeking aDirector of Employee Health and Safety (Remote)who will provide strategic and operational leadership for START's Occupational Health and Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) program across START's clinical operations. This role is accountable for the design, documentation, standardization, implementation, and day-to-day execution of programs that ensure a safe environment for employees, patients, and research activities while maintaining up-to-date compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

The Director ensures adherence to OSHA, USP <797/800>, NIOSH, drug handling guidance, EPA requirements, and research standards. Given START's focus on oncology clinical research, this role also encompasses compliance touchpoints relevant to investigational product handling, hazardous drug exposure, and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and ICH guidelines as they intersect with site safety obligations.

This role establishes and maintains enterprise-wide EHS standards, policies, and procedures governing areas such as drug storage and handling, PPE, fit testing, hazardous material and chemical management, and workplace incident response.

Partnering cross-functionally with Operations/Clinical Leadership, HR, and Compliance, this role translates regulatory and compliance requirements into practical, scalable processes that integrate seamlessly into site operations. The Director will also support select compliance program initiatives under the direction of the Vice President, Compliance and General Counsel, serving as an additional resource for enterprise-wide compliance priorities. The role is responsible for proactive risk identification, incident response, and continuous improvement of safety performance. Success is measured by reduced risk exposure, strong compliance outcomes, and seamless support of business objectives.

This is a remote role. The salary range for this role is $135,000 - $155,000.However, base pay may vary depending on multiple individualized factors including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Work Schedule:

Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm

Essential Responsibilities

Health & Safety (EHS) Compliance

  • Develop, own, and lead a national EHS strategy aligned with organizational growth and operational complexity.
  • Design, implement, and maintain EHS program aligned with OSHA and applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
  • Build and operationalize standardized EHS program across all U.S. sites, ensuring consistency while accommodating state-specific requirements.
  • Ensure compliance across START's clinical, including clinical hazard protocols specific to oncology research settings such as needlestick/bloodborne pathogen exposure response, chemotherapy and hazardous drug spill response, aerosolizing agent exposure, and post-exposure pathways.
  • Lead site assessments, audits, and inspections; implement corrective actions proactively.
  • Maintain all required regulatory reporting and documentation, including OSHA logs and incident records.
  • Provide executive-level reporting on risk, compliance, and safety performance.

Occupational Health

  • Build and manage occupational health programs including injury prevention, case management, return-to-work processes, fitness for duty, and medical surveillance programs.
  • Partner with HR and third-party vendors on workplace accommodations, fitness-for-duty assessments, and employee health-related compliance matters.
  • Coordinate with occupational health providers, workers' compensation carriers, and third-party vendors.
  • Support leaders in responding to workplace injuries or health concerns with clear, compliant processes.

Risk Management & Incident Response

  • Lead investigations into workplace incidents, near misses, and safety concerns.
  • Identify trends and implement preventive strategies to reduce risk exposure.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective and preventive actions, tracking findings through to verified closure — supporting movement toward a high-reliability operating environment.
  • Maintain a robust near-miss and incident reporting culture; ensure follow-up actions are documented, assigned, and resolved, not merely logged.
  • Oversee emergency preparedness and response planning across U.S. locations.

Training & Safety Culture

  • Design, implement, and deliver role-based safety and occupational health training for all employees and supervisors, including new hire EHS onboarding, annual safety competency assessments, and training plans tailored to clinical hazard exposure levels.
  • Embed a culture of accountability and proactive risk identification aligned with START values.
  • Ensure onboarding includes essential safety and health training components; establish and maintain role-specific training matrices.

Operational Partnership

  • Partner with Operations, Clinical Leadership, HR, and Compliance to integrate EHS into workflows and service delivery.
  • Support new site openings, program expansions, and operational changes with safety and environmental assessments.
  • Provide practical, field-ready guidance to managers to ensure compliance without creating operational burden.
  • Support compliance program projects and initiatives as directed by the Vice President, Compliance and General Counsel, contributing subject matter expertise and implementation capacity.

Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish and track key safety and occupational health metrics (e.g., incident rates, lost time, near-miss frequency, compliance completion, CAPA closure rates).
  • Provide regular updates and executive summaries to leadership.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety while supporting efficient operations.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health, Occupational Health, Safety, or related field.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in EHS, occupational health, or workplace safety.
  • Demonstrated experience building and operationalizing EHS programs in a multi-site environment; healthcare, clinical research, or life sciences setting strongly preferred.
  • Experience managing clinical safety hazards, including hazardous drug handling, bloodborne pathogen programs, and post-exposure response protocols.

Preferred Education and Experience:

  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Occupational Health Nurse (OHN), or similar credential.
  • OSHA 30-hour training or equivalent certifications.
  • Familiarity with GCP/ICH guidelines and the intersection of clinical trial operations and site safety obligations.

Physical & Travel Requirements:

  • Travel: Required to travel up to 50% of the time across START's U.S. site network.
  • Sitting: Must be able to sit for extended periods of time.
  • Standing: Must be able to stand for extended periods of time.
  • Bending: Must be able to reach overhead, at shoulder level, or bend to perform tasks.
  • Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Frequent use of computer, keyboard, and mouse.

Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) $70K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LMHC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.

  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

jobs.title: Director, Accounting
jobs.excerpt: Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success.
jobs.description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We’re looking for a Director, Accounting to own day-to-day accounting and treasury operations, reporting to the Controller.

The impact you’ll make:

A Mission Lane customer trusts that when they make a payment, it’s recorded right, that their balance reflects reality, and that the company behind their card is solid enough to keep showing up for them next month and the month after that. None of that happens on its own. It’s built close by close, reconciliation by reconciliation, by an accounting team getting the details exactly right. The Director, Accounting owns that foundation, keeping the numbers behind every customer’s progress ready to stand up to scrutiny.

In your first year, you’ll take full operational ownership of the day-to-day close and treasury accounting, tightening the close calendar and refining internal controls, audit readiness, and AI-enabled workflows toward IPO readiness demands. You’ll do that by:

  • Leading the month-end close, from pre-close prep through balance sheet reconciliations and flux analysis, shrinking the calendar as you progress
  • Owning the monthly consolidation across our multi-entity structure, keeping intercompany eliminations clean and GAAP compliance airtight
  • Directing the annual financial statement audit as our primary external liaison, managing the PBC list and keeping the whole lifecycle on schedule
  • Serving as the go-to partner for our external tax advisors and for Treasury on settlement accounting, restricted cash classifications, and reserve calculations
  • Bringing AI agents into journal entries, reconciliations, and variance reporting, turning the close into something faster and sharper rather than just another deadline
  • Building and developing a small, high-performing accounting team, working alongside them as a player-coach rather than directing from a distance

You’ll thrive in this role if:

  • You’ve run a multi-entity close from the inside and know exactly where the friction points hide.
  • You get real satisfaction from turning a messy reconciliation into a clean one, and from teaching someone else how to do the same.
  • You can lead a team through real process and culture change without losing their trust, even when the change touches how they’ve worked for years.
  • You see AI as a way to make your team’s work better, not a threat to it, and know how to bring skeptics along.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Active CPA and a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
  • 10+ years of progressive accounting and financial management experience, including 5+ years leading a team
  • Deep, hands-on experience with month-end close, financial consolidation, and GAAP compliance in a multi-entity organization
  • Direct experience leading external financial statement audits end to end, including PBC management
  • Working knowledge of the COSO framework and PCAOB standards related to ICFR, with experience designing and testing internal controls
  • Proficiency with NetSuite or a comparable enterprise ERP, plus advanced Excel

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in financial services, consumer lending, or credit card issuing and servicing, especially with sponsor bank models, card networks, or payment processors
  • Experience with Snowflake, SQL, or a BI tool like Tableau
  • A track record of bringing AI or automation into accounting workflows

Compensation:

Annual full-time starting base salary range: $158,000 - $213,000

This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs.

Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.

About Mission Lane:

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

It all started with a realization: nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit. Most traditional credit card companies either overlook or overcharge this group because they have less-than-perfect credit scores or no scores at all. We decided this just wouldn’t do.

In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores.

Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

Our commitment to a workplace built on respect and dignity is guided by our core value of Unity. We believe that everyone plays a vital role in our shared purpose, and we actively cultivate an environment where all individuals have the opportunity to do their best work. By fostering a culture of empathy and collaboration, we create a strong sense of belonging and support for every team member.

Mission Lane is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status.

Mission Lane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants who need them for medical or religious reasons, as required by law. Applicants can initiate an accommodation request by contacting .

Mission Lane is not sponsoring new applicant employment authorization and please, no third-party recruiters.

Our cardholders trust us with their financial well-being, and this trust starts with the integrity of the people on our team. We're looking for team members who share our dedication to transparency and truth. Please verify that the information in your application is accurate and complete.

Providing any information to Mission Lane that is not completely truthful at any point during the application or hiring process may result in removal from the hiring process, disqualification from future opportunities, withdrawal of an offer or other sanctions for candidates and, in addition for employees, disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

jobs.title: VP of Software Engineering
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT NOOKSNooks is pioneering Classified-Infrastructure-as-a-Service (CIaaS) — designing, building, and operating Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and other secured, classified environments for the defense and national security community.
jobs.description:
ABOUT NOOKS

Nooks is pioneering Classified-Infrastructure-as-a-Service (CIaaS) — designing, building, and operating Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and other secured, classified environments for the defense and national security community. We work with the agencies, contractors, and mission-driven organizations that keep the nation safe, delivering the physical infrastructure that makes classified work possible. We’re growing fast, operating across multiple markets, and building a company that takes both the mission and the business seriously.

About the Role

You will lead software engineering at Nooks and own the technical vision for everything we build. That covers three things: the software we deliver under government contract, the platform our site teams and internal functions run on, and the AI strategy that shapes both. AI is not a side initiative here. It is in the products that win us contracts, and Nooks intends to be an industry leader in how we leverage modern AI. You will report to the CEO, sit on the executive leadership team, and set direction rather than receive it. You will be building the function while running it. The team is small today, the operating model is yours to define, and the plan for how it scales is a deliverable rather than a given. Priorities will shift as contracts land and as the business grows into new sites and new lines. You will need to hold a durable technical direction while making short-term calls with incomplete information, and you will be expected to bring answers instead of waiting for them.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Organization and Delivery

  • Lead, develop, and scale a software engineering organization accountable for delivery, quality, security, reliability, and operational outcomes based on internal and external customers
  • Define the operating model that moves the team from project-based execution to outcome-based ownership, with clear intake, prioritization, and delivery cadence.
  • Build a strong team through deliberate hiring, training, and retention, developing the engineers you have while adding the capabilities you need.
  • Establish engineering metrics and reporting that give the executive team real visibility into velocity, quality, AI adoption, and business impact.

AI Strategy and Adoption

  • Own the AI strategy across Nooks, spanning the AI capabilities in our delivered products and the integration of AI into how the company works.
  • Drive measurable AI adoption across internal functions, accountable not just for shipping capability but for changing how teams actually operate.
  • Rebuild how Nooks captures, structures, and retrieves institutional knowledge so expertise scales beyond the people who hold it.
  • Own AI governance for the software portfolio, including data handling, model use, and evaluation, coordinating with IT/Cyber where network security apply.

Government Contract Delivery and Capture

  • Own delivery against awarded software contracts, including scope, schedule, technical quality, and customer confidence in our capabilities.
  • Run awarded work as a managed line with visible economics, owning cost, staffing, and utilization against the commitment (and EBITA expectations).
  • Represent Nooks engineering and AI capability directly to government customers, in delivery reviews and in pursuit conversations.
  • Support Growth on software pursuits by shaping technical approach, staffing models, and cost inputs, and by converting delivered work into past performance Nooks can compete on.

Internal Technology Strategy, Platform, and Investment

  • Set the technology strategy and architecture roadmap for everything the team builds, including systems that may deploy into customer environments.
  • Own the platform our site teams, Operations, and internal functions depend on to manage our spaces, our members, and our customer contracts.
  • Make and defend build-versus-buy decisions, integrating commercial systems where they fit and building only where Nooks gains real advantage.
  • Build the business case for engineering investment, including headcount, tooling, and vendor decisions, and manage the portfolio against it.

What Success Looks Like in This Role

Software delivery is predictable enough that leadership stops asking for status and starts asking what else the team can take on, with awarded work running against known economics rather than best effort. AI shows up in workflows that measurably change, and in product capability the customer can see, with tangible adoption you can point to rather than describe. The platform our site teams use is in production and reducing work, not sitting in a roadmap. Growth brings you into software pursuits early because your input changes whether Nooks bids and how it prices, and government customers treat you as the credible technical voice for the company. The executive team relies on you for the technology and AI direction of the business, and the plan for how the function scales exists, is funded, and is being executed.

Cross-Functional Expectations

You will work with the CEO on technology and AI direction, with Growth on pursuits and customer engagement, with Operations and the site teams who depend on what you build, with IT/Cyber to manage network and infrastructure dependencies, and with Product on where physical and digital offerings meet. Operations for what your team ships are yours, run in partnership with IT/Cyber. You will also work with Finance on the economics of delivered work and the case for engineering investment. Externally you will hold technical relationships with government customers and manage the vendor and partner ecosystem across the software stack.

The Skillset

  • 8+ years in software engineering with progressive leadership responsibility, including ownership of a full engineering or software product function.
  • Experience leading software delivery to the USG, with direct exposure to federal customers and the constraints that come with them.
  • A Command of modern AI practice, including large language models (LLMs), agentic frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), orchestration, and AI governance.
  • Experience owning delivery economics, including cost, staffing, and utilization against a fixed commitment, and built the business case for technology investment.
  • Experience building and leading an engineering organization, including operating model, hiring, and the shift toward outcome-based delivery.
  • Demonstrable experience managing customer and cross-functional relationships at the executive level.

Preferred:

  • Experience in defense, national security, or another regulated environment with clearance, compliance, or controlled-data constraints.
  • Software capture experience, including technical approach and cost input on federal proposals.
  • Experience delivering software for field-based or operational users.
  • Active security clearance.

Eligibility & Clearance

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. An active security clearance is preferred. All candidates must be eligible for and committed to obtaining and maintaining a U.S. government security clearance as a condition of employment.

Salary Range for all departments

Salary Range
$230,000—$275,000 USD

As a Strategic Accounts Customer Success Manager, you will be the face of Motive for our largest customers. As a member of a fast-paced and tight-knit team, you will help support product and business development to satisfy customer needs along with developing internal tools to help the business gain scale.

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop strong working relationships at multiple management levels within the customer accounts, including C Suite relationships
